key_insight: VecTile uses passive silicone nubs to convert normal and shear forces into distinguishable pressure patterns, enabling low-cost three-axis tactile sensing.
engineering_relevance: The flexible, 6 mm-thin sensor costs under US$35 for a 4×4 array and provides contact-force feedback for robotic manipulation.
method: Combine a piezoresistive layer with passive silicone nubs.
Validate force-to-pressure transduction using finite element analysis and hardware experiments.
Calibrate force estimates and test transfer from flat to curved configurations.
evidence_signal: Controlled single-taxel tests over 1–5 N normal force and up to 1.5 N shear force yielded RMSEs of 0.39 N and 0.16 N for normal and shear forces, respectively.
watch_item: Reported force errors come from controlled single-taxel tests; full-array accuracy under simultaneous contacts is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: VecTile: A Low-Cost Flexible Tactile Array for 3-DoF Force Sensing
